signals.title: AUD/NZD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: AUD/NZD trades at 1.2547, sitting rich against its BEER fair-value model at 1.2409 (z=+1.99σ). In the weekly currency performance matrix, AUD leads the G10 basket with a +0.885% average gain across 4 pairs, while NZD anchors the table as the primary laggard down -0.547% across 4 pairs, creating an active bilateral spread of 1.432%. Fundamental momentum confirms the spread: Australia's policy rate sits at 4.6% following persistent tightening pressures, while New Zealand's overnight benchmark stands at 2.75%, leaving an expansive cash carry spread favoring the Aussie. ESI data confirms divergence, with NZD printing persistent misses at -17.1 versus AUD at -7.1. Trade bias: Long AUD/NZD; cross-currency momentum and yield advantages reinforce the trend. Catalyst: Australia PPI at 00:30 UTC — forecast 1.0% q/q. Risk: Bilateral spread compresses back below 0.80% if commodity demand abruptly softens.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Extreme + Vol Skew Ahead of ECB
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1146, held cleanly below its descending SMA20 (1.1209), SMA50 (1.1412), and SMA200 (1.1569) moving average cluster. Speculative positioning shows leveraged funds heavily net short EUR at -94,138 contracts (CFTC, week ending Oct 20), placing EUR net length in the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.72. Implied volatility runs at 6.5% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.0%, yielding an elevated 2.5-point volatility risk premium that reflects hedging demand ahead of the ECB policy announcement and leadership transition news. Meanwhile, retail positioning sits at 87% long on Retail sentiment data, diverging sharply from the institutional short overhang and establishing contrarian vulnerability. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; technical downtrend and institutional short positioning cap recovery attempts. Catalyst: ECB Interest Rate Decision at 13:15 UTC — hold expected. Risk: A hawkish hold from the ECB triggers a short-squeeze across crowded institutional shorts toward 1.1250.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Trend Extension + Retail Extreme
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.25, extending its structured downtrend below the SMA20 (9.462), SMA50 (9.406), and SMA200 (9.504) moving average cluster. The latest daily candle formed a wide-range bearish expansion bar that stretched spot 2.73 ATR below its falling 20-day average. Retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data displays an extreme one-sided stance with 100% of community accounts positioned long, attempting to catch the extended downswing. This positioning runs contrary to the ongoing technical regime and fundamental rate dynamics, where Norges Bank maintains a restrictive 4.5% policy stance against Fed funds at 4.0%. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK; technical momentum aligned against retail positioning extreme. Catalyst: US Core PCE Price Index at 12:30 UTC — forecast 0.2% m/m, 3.1% y/y. Risk: An upside US PCE inflation surprise lifts broad dollar yields and triggers a technical mean-reversion toward the 9.406 SMA50.
